precedents.title: SB 887 requires environmental review for every new data center
precedents.what: Signed in September 2026 as part of a seven-bill package. All new data center projects must undergo CEQA review. A faster path requires a commitment to fully renewable power within five years, water-efficient cooling and a community benefits agreement.
precedents.lesson: San José's Uniform Standards can require the same three commitments as a condition of any Special Use Permit. The Rules Committee already directed staff to support SB 887.

precedents.title: SB 886 directs regulators to keep data center power costs off household bills
precedents.what: Part of the same September 2026 package. State regulators must write rules so that the public does not bear the cost of data centers' energy needs.
precedents.lesson: Until the CPUC rules exist, the city can ask each applicant to show who pays for its substation and transmission upgrades.

precedents.title: SB 57 orders a study of data center cost shifts by January 2027
precedents.what: Signed October 11, 2025, after its proposed special data center tariff was stripped out. The CPUC must publish an assessment of whether data centers shift grid costs onto other customers by January 1, 2027.
precedents.lesson: The CPUC findings arrive in early 2027. That is a reasonable point to pause approvals until they are in hand.

precedents.title: Data center water-use reporting (AB 93) was vetoed
precedents.what: The Governor vetoed a 2025 bill that would have required data centers to report water use. No statewide water disclosure applies.
precedents.lesson: Only 3 of the 11 San José data center filings name a cooling method. The city can require water-use figures itself.

precedents.place: Bay Area Air Quality Management District
precedents.title: 20 groups petition BAAQMD over data center diesel generators
precedents.what: The Center for Biological Diversity, Sierra Club, SPUR and others note that Bay Area data centers can have 20 to 50 diesel backup generators per site. Operators self-report emergencies and need not disclose emissions. The petition asks for public reporting, single-source permitting per site, tighter limits on emergency use, and battery alternatives.
precedents.lesson: The council can formally support the petition and require battery or clean backup in its own standards.

precedents.title: PG&E's data center queue swings from 5 GW to 12.7 GW
precedents.what: PG&E reported a 12.7 GW data center pipeline in July 2026. Only 490 MW had signed interconnection agreements, and the prior quarter's figure was revised down to 5.1 GW.
precedents.lesson: Speculative requests are common. San José's 880 MW reservation deserves the same scrutiny before ratepayers fund upgrades.

precedents.title: Next door, Santa Clara's grid now caps new data centers
precedents.what: Santa Clara has 55 operating data centers. A city spokesperson confirmed its grid caps new ones, and councilmembers said proposals have been turned down over grid limits while utility upgrades run to 2029.
precedents.lesson: Santa Clara shows what saturation looks like. Without a cap, San José absorbs the overflow.

precedents.title: Imperial Valley pauses data centers after public outcry
precedents.what: After residents packed hearings over a proposed $10 billion campus, the Board of Supervisors extended a pause on data center development through mid-2027. Several cities in the region are weighing their own moratoriums or bans.
precedents.lesson: A time-limited pause while standards are written is an established California tool.

precedents.title: Indianapolis bars new data centers through 2027
precedents.what: The City-County Council voted 23-1 on Aug 10, 2026, and the Metropolitan Development Commission voted 6-0 on Aug 19, to stop new data center projects through the end of 2027 while regulations are written. Three previously approved projects are exempt.
precedents.lesson: A large-city precedent for pausing new applications while letting approved projects proceed.

precedents.title: Tucson council unanimously stops Amazon-linked 'Project Blue'
precedents.what: On Aug 6, 2025, the council voted to end negotiations on annexation and a development agreement, citing water and electricity use and intense public opposition. The mayor began drafting an ordinance to limit future data centers.
precedents.lesson: Councils can decline development agreements on resource grounds even after negotiations begin.

precedents.title: Court voids the largest planned data center campus over public notice
precedents.what: A circuit judge voided the Digital Gateway rezonings in August 2025 because hearing notices failed state and county requirements. The Virginia Court of Appeals unanimously upheld the ruling on March 31, 2026.
precedents.lesson: Notice and hearing procedure matters. San José residents have said projects were approved without public input, and Council Policy 6-30 outreach should be applied in full.

precedents.title: Virginia's legislative auditor: household bills could rise $14 to $37 a month
precedents.what: JLARC found Virginia's roughly 340 data centers need about 5 GW, with demand expected to double in 15 years. Unconstrained growth could add $14 to $37 a month to a typical Dominion residential bill by 2040.
precedents.lesson: The most-studied data center market in the U.S. projects real household costs. Ask PG&E for the equivalent analysis for San José's 880 MW.

precedents.title: Oregon's POWER Act puts data centers in their own rate class
precedents.what: HB 3546 (2025) has regulators create a separate rate class for customers of 20 MW or more. It requires contracts of at least 10 years with minimum payments, even if the facility uses less power than it reserved.
precedents.lesson: Minimum-payment contracts protect households if projects underuse their reservation. This is a model to urge on the CPUC under SB 886.

precedents.title: Texas lets its grid operator cut data centers off in emergencies
precedents.what: SB 6 (June 2025) requires new loads of 75 MW or more to accept remote disconnection during load-shed emergencies. It also requires them to pay at least $100,000 for interconnection studies and to disclose on-site backup generation.
precedents.lesson: If the grid sheds data centers in emergencies, their diesel generators run. Generator disclosure belongs in every San José filing.

precedents.title: Memphis: xAI ran gas turbines before getting an air permit
precedents.what: Residents and the Southern Environmental Law Center documented dozens of turbines operating at xAI's data center ahead of permitting. The health department permitted 15 turbines in July 2025, and the NAACP appealed.
precedents.lesson: On-site generation is an air-quality decision. Require BAAQMD permits and a health risk assessment before land-use approval.
